messages:
maya: Heads-up — SpectraHealth (dedicated) reported p95 token latency spikes starting ~01:00 UTC after our last kernel-roll. They want token_budget and queue limits increased temporarily while we investigate. attaching snapshot and high-level ask. :wave:

jonathan: Can you paste the p95/p99 numbers and the model variant? Also which kernel/version is on their fleet?

maya: p50~45ms p95~720ms p99~1.2s for text-gen (curie-quant-v2). Kernel shows `kernel-4.3.1` on their hosts. Observed sustained token inflight ~3x normal. Snapshot: https://internal.spectra/shot/ae3c (access granted)

arjun: thx. Quick read: sounds like queue pileup + suboptimal kernel choice for long-context tokens. Before changing routing, we can try a conservative per-customer token_budget bump and tighten queue timeout to drain long requests faster. Proposed config snippet to apply to their Dedicated pool: 

```json
{
  "customer_id": "spectrahealth",
  "batching": {
    "token_budget": 120000,
    "max_queue_tokens": 8192,
    "queue_timeout_ms": 80,
    "priority_policy": "latency_preferred"
  }
}
```

liam: quick q — token_budget 120k is per-GPU or per-pool? we should be explicit. also what about kv-cache pinning? their workload is multi-session which benefits from cache.

arjun: good call — that token_budget is pool-wide reserve for spectrahealth across the dedicated shard. we should keep per-host caps: `per_host_max_tokens: 32768`. for KV cache we'll keep `kv_prefetch=true` and set `kv_cache_age_ms` to 15m to avoid thrash.

jonathan: ran a small canary applying the above to one host with kernel-3.9.7 and one with kernel-4.3.1 to compare. results (10k requests over 30m):
- host A (3.9.7): p95 token latency 210ms, p99 340ms, throughput +12%
- host B (4.3.1): p95 token latency 680ms, p99 980ms, throughput -4%

jonathan: attaching lightweight flamegraphs and profiler slices — suspicion: `matmul` kernel fallback on 4.3.1 causes high tail for longer sequences. also queue_timeout magic reduced tail but increased d/c rate for some long responses.

maya: Spectra asked for an immediate mitigation window of 24hrs. They prefer config change over rolling back kernel. can we do the pool-wide token_budget bump + per-host cap and tighten queue timeout?

arjun: yes. propose rollout plan:
1) apply config to one dedicated shard (canary) — tonight 23:00 UTC for 1hr
2) monitor p95/p99, inflight tokens, and cache hit rate via console dashboards + quick smoke queries
3) if stable, expand to rest of their shards in 3 phases (30m stagger)

liam: add limits to avoid starving other tenants on same physical infra: `global_token_hardcap: 200000` and `per_customer_burst_window: 60s` so bursts don't blow out GPU mem.

jonathan: implemented canary config and kicked off canary run. small note: I tweaked `queue_timeout_ms` to 70ms (slightly more aggressive than arjun's 80ms) — lowered p99 by ~120ms on host A. logs: 

```
[2026-03-17T23:00:12Z] applied config spectrahealth.canary -> token_budget=120000 per_host_max=32768 queue_timeout_ms=70
[2026-03-17T23:15:04Z] inflight_tokens: avg=14200 peak=28400 cache_hit=0.82 p95=198ms p99=321ms
[2026-03-17T23:45:01Z] inflight_tokens: avg=16000 peak=30010 cache_hit=0.80 p95=205ms p99=330ms
```

maya: :thumbsup: this looks promising. can you summarize expected customer-visible changes so I can tell support what to say?

arjun: TL;DR for support: reduced p95/p99 tail for most requests; short increase in small reject/drops for extremely long token streams (>16k) due to tighter queue timeout; KV cache warmup retained so multi-session latency should improve. recommend telling them we applied temporary burst increase and will revert or further tune after 24h.

liam: created infra ticket INF-4921 linking the canary logs and config PR: https://git.redwood/inference/configs/pull/832. set SLO watch on spectrahealth.dedicated.* for the next 24h.

jonathan: one more perf note — long-term fix is to re-evaluate kernel selection for 4.3.1 hosts and maybe pin a different matmul kernel or force alternate kernel path for sequences > 1024. filed PERF-2113 for kernel selection investigation.

maya: thanks all. I'll update the customer and close loop with support. please post any anomalies in this thread. :eyes:

sre-bot: Reminder: scheduled canary window ends at 2026-03-18T00:00:00Z. Automated alerts will post to #incidents if p99 > 800ms for >5min.
